clue.text: Head-holding in court

definitions.meaning: in boxing and wrestling slang a head trapped under an opponent's arm is said to be 'in ...', held helpless
the Court of ... was the Lord Chancellor's court of equity in England

explanation.surface: A grappling hold seen in a courtroom scuffle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word here, but it also echoes the old phrase 'in chancery' for a fighter's head held fast under an opponent's arm.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are the same word: a wrestling hold of the head, and the old English equity court of the Lord Chancellor.

clue.text: .The Floral Universe?

parts.note: one word names both the whole ordered universe and a garden flower with daisy-like heads

explanation.surface: A grand title for an entire world of flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: The same word is the ordered universe and a garden plant of the daisy family.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means the ordered universe and is also a daisy-like annual garden flower.

clue.text: He writes 'to the French god

parts.note: au is French for 'to the'
Thor is the Norse god of thunder

explanation.surface: A man sending letters to a French deity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the French' means 'to the' in French, which is AU.
explanation.definitionFit: A writer is someone who writes books.

clue.text: Does this feature bar one from the Dunmow Flitch?

definitions.text: Does this feature bar one from the Dunmow Flitch?

parts.words: Does this feature bar one from the Dunmow Flitch?
parts.note: the Dunmow Flitch, a side of bacon, goes to a couple who have not quarrelled in a year and a day, so one angry remark disqualifies

explanation.surface: Asking whether a puzzle disqualifies one from an old Essex marriage prize.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dunmow Flitch is an Essex custom awarding bacon to a couple with no quarrel for a year and a day; a 'cross word' would rule them out.
explanation.definitionFit: A cross word, an angry remark, would lose the bacon; the puzzle is a grid of such words.

clue.text: It enables anyone to stage a come-back

definitions.text: It enables anyone to stage a come-back

parts.words: It enables anyone to stage a come-back
parts.note: a travel document that pays for the journey home as well as the journey out

explanation.surface: Something that lets a faded star make a comeback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stage a come-back' suggests a performer's return; it means a travel pass that covers the trip back.
explanation.definitionFit: A ticket covering both the outward journey and the return trip.

clue.text: "I had rather live With cheese and ——in a windmill" (I Henry IV)

definitions.text: I had rather live With cheese and ——in a windmill

parts.words: I had rather live With cheese and ——in a windmill
parts.note: Hotspur's line in Shakespeare's Henry IV Part 1, complaining of Glendower's talk, names a pungent bulb eaten with cheese

explanation.surface: A quotation from Shakespeare with one word blanked out for the solver to supply.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints '1 Henry IV', Shakespeare's Henry IV Part 1; Hotspur says he would rather live on cheese and a strong-smelling bulb in a windmill than listen to Glendower.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word in Hotspur's speech is the pungent bulb, a smelly food that suits a miserable life in a windmill.

clue.text: She has a horse and three quarters!

parts.note: a horse is a gee-gee, and gee is the name of the letter G
north, east and south are three of the four compass quarters

explanation.surface: A woman who owns a horse and three-quarters of something.
explanation.walkthrough: A horse is a 'gee' in nursery talk, and gee is how the letter G is said; the three quarters are compass points N, E, S.
explanation.definitionFit: Agnes is a woman's name, so it stands for a she.

clue.text: Bounty from the nineteenth capital, say ?

indicators.note: say tells you the phrase large ess is spoken and its sound gives the word

parts.note: S is the nineteenth letter, and a capital S is a large ess

explanation.surface: Generous gifts from some unnamed nineteenth capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like a city but is a capital letter; the nineteenth is S, so 'large ess', which when said sounds like the word for generosity.
explanation.definitionFit: Largesse is generous giving, a bounty handed out freely.

clue.text: In the hunt, sit back when beat

indicators.note: in says the turned word goes inside the word for the hunt

parts.note: a hunt is a chase

indicators.note: back says the letters of sit are read from right to left

explanation.surface: During a hunt, a rider sits back in the saddle when beaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns SIT into TIS, and 'In' puts it inside CHASE; 'when' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To chastise is to punish, especially by beating.

clue.text: Start journey to place by river

parts.note: to place something is to set it down
the Forth is the Scottish river flowing into the Firth of Forth

explanation.surface: Setting off on a trip to somewhere beside a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is a link word placing one piece beside the other; the Forth is a Scottish river.
explanation.definitionFit: To set out on a journey, a phrasal verb meaning to begin travelling.

clue.text: Son of a 'tailor and an engineer, a painter

parts.note: taken as written
RE stands for the Royal Engineers, the British Army's engineering corps

explanation.surface: A family tree: a tailor's son, an engineer, and a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: Andrea del Sarto, the Florentine painter, took his name from his father's trade: 'del Sarto' means 'of the tailor'. 'painter' confirms who is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: The Renaissance painter Andrea del Sarto was named for his father, a tailor (sarto in Italian).

clue.text: In certain cases about one minute — that makes one guilty ?

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: about says the cases go round the next pieces

parts.note: crates are a kind of packing case
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: In some legal cases, a minute's delay is what convicts a man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts CRATES round I and MIN; 'that' is a link word. 'cases' suggests law cases but means packing cases.
explanation.definitionFit: To incriminate is to make someone appear guilty of a crime.

clue.text: Tramps 'ere in the reeds

indicators.note: a Cockney 'ere for 'here' drops its first letter, so the tramps word loses its aitch the same way

parts.note: hoboes are tramps or vagrants

explanation.surface: Vagrants sleeping among the rushes by the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ere is 'here' with the H dropped, Cockney fashion, and it tells you to drop the H from HOBOES. 'reeds' are reed instruments, not plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Oboes are double-reed woodwind instruments, so musicians call them reeds.

clue.text: Like a phoenix from the flames about to point the way up

definitions.text: Like a phoenix from the flames

parts.note: re means about or concerning
N is north, a point of the compass
an ascent is a way up a slope

explanation.surface: A phoenix rising from the fire and soaring skywards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'point' is a compass point, here N for north; 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Renascent means being reborn, as the mythical bird is reborn from its own ashes.

clue.text: Spirits in form of nightly bumpers perhaps ?

definitions.text: Spirits in form of nightly bumpers perhaps

parts.words: Spirits in form of nightly bumpers perhaps
parts.note: ghosts that make thumps and bangs in the dark, the noisy German 'knocking spirits'

explanation.surface: Ghosts taking the shape of things that go bump in the night.
explanation.walkthrough: The German name means 'noisy ghost': spirits blamed for knocks and crashes in the night, the 'bumps' of the old prayer about things that go bump in the night.
explanation.definitionFit: These are mischievous ghosts said to throw objects and make knocking noises in a house.

clue.text: Very detailed though it may appear to be a real tangle

definitions.text: Very detailed though it may appear to be a real tangle

parts.words: Very detailed though it may appear to be a real tangle
parts.note: intricate work with many parts can look like a muddle to an onlooker

explanation.surface: Something so intricate that it looks hopelessly knotted.
explanation.walkthrough: Something worked out in great detail can look like a mess of complications.
explanation.definitionFit: Elaborate means worked out with great care and much detail, intricate.

clue.text: Stocky in a hedgy way?

definitions.meaning: a stocky person is short and broad
a hedge is planted with its shrubs close together, densely set

explanation.surface: A heavily built man who behaves evasively.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hedgy' suggests hedging or evasion, but means like a hedge, whose plants are set thick.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavily built, and also planted or growing closely together like a hedge.

clue.text: Nuts! You'll need them !

definitions.meaning: nuts here means mad, an exclamation of disbelief
to open nuts you need a pair of nutcrackers

explanation.surface: An exasperated cry, followed by a warning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nuts!' is an exclamation meaning mad; the second part means you need crackers to deal with nuts.
explanation.definitionFit: Crackers is slang for mad, and crackers are the tools that open nuts.

clue.text: Anglo-French Manx charger is out of action

indicators.note: a Manx cat has no tail, so the word for the charger loses its final letter

parts.note: a charger is a cavalry or war horse
a war horse in mixed English and French would be a horse 'de combat', of combat

explanation.surface: A tailless war horse from the Isle of Man is no longer fit to fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Manx' refers to the tailless Manx cat, so HORSE loses its tail to give HORS; 'Anglo-French' adds the French DE COMBAT, making a half-English 'war horse'.
explanation.definitionFit: This French phrase, used in English, describes a soldier disabled and unable to fight.

clue.text: The burden of the carol-singer we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the singer's word is spoken and its sound gives the answer

parts.note: the waits were bands of Christmas street singers and players

explanation.surface: The refrain of a carol singer's song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'burden' looks like the chorus of a song, matching 'carol-singer', but it means a load. The waits were Christmas carol singers.
explanation.definitionFit: A weight is a heavy load, a burden carried.

clue.text: No charity item in Cardinal's wardrobe list

parts.note: a hat is an item of clothing
cardinal red is the deep scarlet of a cardinal's robes

explanation.surface: A churchman's inventory of clothes lacking any gift to the poor.
explanation.walkthrough: A list of a cardinal's wardrobe would read 'hat, red', the famous red hat; 'charity' means Christian love, not giving.
explanation.definitionFit: Charity in its Biblical sense is love, so its absence is loathing.

clue.text: Make clean copy of this masonry

indicators.note: make tells you to build something new out of the letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: An instruction to produce a fair copy of a description of stonework.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make' is the anagram signal: the letters of CLEAN COPY are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyclopean masonry is built of huge irregular stones, as if laid by the one-eyed giants of myth.

clue.text: Out and about, offending propriety

parts.note: taken as written
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Someone out on the town behaving badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is RE, as in 're your letter'.
explanation.definitionFit: Outré is French for beyond the bounds, unconventional and shocking.

clue.text: Benedicite, they are all bidden

parts.note: the Latin canticle Benedicite opens by calling on all the works of the Lord, 'omnia ... Domini', to bless him

explanation.surface: A remark that in the hymn Benedicite everyone is invited.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Latin Benedicite 'omnia opera' (all ye works) are bidden to bless the Lord, and opera is the Latin plural of opus, a work.
explanation.definitionFit: In Latin the word is the plural of opus, meaning works, the very things the canticle summons.

clue.text: Lady has different hat' for this sort of dress

parts.note: she is the pronoun for a lady

indicators.note: different says the letters of the headgear word appear in another order

explanation.surface: A woman wearing a new hat to go with a particular frock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'different' turns HAT into ATH, which follows SHE.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheath is a close-fitting, straight dress.

clue.text: Spied in the House or in a tea-cup

definitions.meaning: a member of the House of Commons calling 'I spy ...' asked for outsiders in the gallery to be removed
in tea-leaf fortune telling, a floating leaf or stalk foretells the arrival of an unknown visitor

explanation.surface: Something glimpsed both in Parliament and in the bottom of a cup of tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I spy strangers' was the Commons formula for clearing the public gallery; a tea stalk floating in a cup traditionally means a visitor is coming.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are an outsider: a non-member in the Commons, and the unexpected visitor foretold by tea leaves.

clue.text: Like a poor matador, suffered from insomnia

definitions.meaning: an unlucky bullfighter is thrown into the air by the bull's horns
a sleepless person turns restlessly all night in bed

explanation.surface: A bullfighter who had a bad day in the ring and then could not sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: One sense is being flung by the bull; the other is the 'tossed and turned' of a sleepless night.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrown by the bull, and also lay turning restlessly in bed all night.

clue.text: Gave Bill the O.K.

parts.note: the Bill is a parliamentary bill, which becomes law when royal approval is given

explanation.surface: Someone telling a man called Bill that all is well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name, but it is a bill in Parliament receiving royal approval.
explanation.definitionFit: To agree or consent, as the sovereign does in giving royal approval to a parliamentary bill.
